To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the amino acid sensor of Saccharomyce cerevisiae is a permease‐like protein that is required for the induction, in response of external amino acids, several genes encoding peptide or amino acid transporters.
the Ssy1–Ptr3–Ssy5 pathway is a novel amino acid sensing pathway that regulates expression of several genes encoding amino acid permeases in Saccharomyce s cerevisiae.
Ssy1p, Ptr3p and Uga35p act together in a signalling pathway required for transcriptional activation of AGP1 and several other genes in response to the presence of amino acids in the environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of a novel pathway in S. cerevisiae, which responds to external amino acids and is required for the transcriptional induction of a number of genes encoding amino acid transporters.
the identification and characterization of the components of a novel pathway activated in response to amino acids in yeast, and with the elucidation of their functions.
the elucidation of a novel pathway for the sensing of amino acids in the environment of yeast cells and with the identification of the proteins participating in this pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pathway is a complex network of interactions between the amino acid permeases, the permease‐like protein Ssy1p, the transcription factor Uga3p, the zinc finger protein Uga35p, and two additional proteins of unknown function, Ptr3p and Ptr5p.
Ptr3p and Uga35p act downstream from Ssy5p, whereas Ptr3p is upstream of Uga35p.
Ssy1p senses external amino acids and transmits the signal to Ptr3p, which in turn transmits it to Ssy5p.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Ssy1p acts as a sensor for external amino acids, that the amino‐terminal tail is a functional element of Ssy1, that Ptr3p lies downstream from Ssy3, that Ssy5p lies downstream from Ptr3 and that Uga35p is a component of the pathway.
the Ssy1 protein is a sensor of amino acids and that the Ptr3 and Ssy5 proteins act downstream from Ssy‐1 and are involved in the transduction of the signal to the nucleus.
Ptr3p and Uga35p act in the same signalling pathway as Ssy1p, whereas Ssy5p is a downstream component of this pathway that acts independently of Uga35p.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ssy1–Ptr3–Ssy5 pathway is a novel amino acid signalling pathway in yeast.
the Ssy1‐Ptr3‐Ssy5 pathway is a novel signalling pathway that controls the expression of several genes encoding amino acid and peptide permeases.
, in addition to Ssy1p, Ptr3p and the Cys‐Zn2 factor Uga35/Dal81p, Ssy5p is an essential component of the amino‐acid sensing pathway in S. cerevisiae.
